label: Ingarden published Quantum Information Theory
description: Paper written in 1976 by the Polish mathematical physicist Roman Ingarden.

sources.quote: For example, a few years ago I found a paper on the subject written in 1976 by the Polish mathematical phy sicist Roman Ingarden [1].

label: Holevo published qubit information result
description: His 1973 result that n quantum bits cannot carry more than n bits of information.

sources.quote: His 1973 resul t that n quantum bits, or qubits for short, cannot carry more than n bits of information is frequently invoked in the modern quantum information theory .

label: Proposed BB84 quantum key distribution
description: In 1984 Bennett and Brassard proposed a protocol for quantum key distribution.

sources.quote: As you know, in 1984 Bennett and Brassard proposed a protocol for quantum key dis- tribution, a way of letting two people, Alice and Bob, share a set of random perfectly correlated bits about which no else has any or hardly any info rmation.

label: Lo and Chau proved QKD security
description: Lo and Chau showed in 1999 how Alice and Bob can proceed to obtain entangled states.

sources.quote: Following this line of reasoning, Lo and Chau showed in 1999 [ 3] how Alice and Bob can proceed in order to obtain (something close to) a set o f entangled states and in this way they proved the security of an entanglement-base d quantum key distribution scheme.

label: Shor and Preskill proved BB84 security
description: Shor and Preskill in 2000 built their security proof of Bennett & Brassard's '84 scheme.

sources.quote: The work by Lo and Chau was the stepping stone on which Shor and Preskill [4] in 2000 built their security proof of Bennett & Brassard's '84 scheme.

label: Published Mixed State Entanglement paper
description: 1996 paper by Bennett et al. on Mixed State Entanglement and Quantum Error Correction.

sources.quote: A ﬁrst example of a mixed entangled state that is is not monogamous but shareable –the term is from Ben Schumacher–, can be found in the 1996 paper by Bennett et al.

label: Bell formulated inequality
description: In the sixties John Bell formulated an inequality that has to be obeyed by any theory that is classical and local.

sources.quote: In the sixties John Bell formulated an inequality that has to be obeyed by any theory that is classical and local [9].

label: Werner published on hidden-variable models
description: Work by Reinhard Werner showing that there exist states which are entangled but do not violate Bell inequalities.

sources.quote: This question has some history , starting with work by Reinhard Werner showing that there exist states, now called Werner st ates which are entangled but do not violate Bell inequalities for any number of local m easurement settings [10].
